minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 2, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on September 2, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 28, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon (arrived at 6:32 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of 54956.9: two cases.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Reardon
arrived at 6:32 p.m.
City Council Minutes  1  September 2, 2014
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two items under CS1. For the
first matter, the Council received an update and gave direction to staff. For the second matter,
staff provided an update and the City Council is reserving the option to return to Closed Session if
need-be after the open session, based on information presented at tonight's meeting.

PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  State Water Resources Control Board Emergency Water Conservation Regulations -
  Presented by El Toro Water District, Moulton-Niguel Water District, and Santa Margarita
  Water District

  The City Council received presentations from Bob Hill, General Manager, El Toro Water District;
  Matt Collings, Moulton-Niguel Water District; and Dan Ferons, General Manager, Santa
  Margarita Water District.

  Victor Gonzalez, M.V.: stated that it appears that the managers of water are the biggest wasters
  of water. He asked questions of the water district representatives relative to penalties and
  procedures and what the community can do to try to steer the state government towards
  construction of more water storage.

 P2.  Presentation by Historian Bob Hayes on the 200th Anniversary of the National Anthem

  The City Council received the presentation from Bob Hayes.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Lynn Hatton Hodson, M.V.: stated that four years ago she ran for CUSD Board of Directors
because she saw a need for change. Mrs. Hatton Hudson announced that she is running for the
School Board again and she outlined some of the accomplishments that have been made at the
district over the last four years.

Amy Hanacek, Capistrano Beach: discussed the positive forward-focus of the CUSD Board of
Directors and she stated that many of the accomplishments were achieved under the guidance of
Board Member Lynn Hatton Hodson.

Margot Ferron, M.V.: announced that Mission Viejo will host a Stand Up To Cancer telecast
viewing party on September 5, 2014, from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community
Center.

City Council Minutes  2  September 2, 2014
 Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: in honor of the men and women of the military, she announced that the
City of Mission Viejo will host a very special ceremony for Patriots Day on September 11 and on
September 12, Mission Viejo High School will host the Mission for the Armed Forces football
game. The community will "welcome home" its Vietnam Veterans on September 20 at the
community center and lastly, Mrs. Bucknum encouraged residents to sign up for the Tee It Up
Fore Marines golf tournament in October.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: warned seniors to beware of billing for paramedic services by
ambulance companies that are required to give a rebate back to the Orange County Fire
Authority. He encouraged seniors to request that Mission Viejo formally object to this practice,
make this a campaign issue for the upcoming election and for Casta del Sol to address the issue
during the upcoming City Council Candidate debate.

Kathy Richardson, M.V.: expressed concern with traffic and speeds on Crown Valley
Parkway. She asked if the City will put up some kind of warning sign that shows the current speed
and will flash if a driver is going too fast.

Courtney Mauss and Miranda Cowdrey, Mission Viejo High School Students and President/Vice
President of Troop 3060 of the International Thespians Society: announced that they hosted a food
drive and raised 37,000 lbs. of food in Mission Viejo last year. They are hosting another food drive
this year and they invited the entire community, local schools and churches to join in their
efforts. They also asked that the City help to get the word out.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated August 8, 2014 in the Amount of $785,652.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  September 2, 2014
 4.  Check Register Dated August 15, 2014 in the Amount of $1,071,350.60

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Claim Against the City - Herbers vs. City of Mission Viejo

  Rejected claim.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

Items 7 and 8 were taken out of order.

8.  Briefing by County of Orange staff on Probation Office to be located at 26030 Acero,
  Highpark, in the City’s BP (Business Park/Industrial) zone

  Mayor Kelley announced that the Council learned this afternoon that the County Board of
  Supervisors will delay action on this matter. She thanked Supervisor Pat Bates for hearing
  the concerns of the City and the residents and for putting a hold on the probation office.

  Steven J. Sentman, Chief Probation Officer, OC Probation Department, Santa Ana:
  provided an overview of the proposed South County Field Service Office and the operations
  and services that would take place at the site.

  The following spoke in opposition to a probation office at the proposed location: Bill
  Arsenean, San Juan Capistrano; Dennis Lumley, M.V.; Michelle Sullivan, M.V.; Lamar
  Kelsoe, M.V.; M. Mahboob Akhter, M.V.; Valorie Green, M.V.; Bill Davies, Irvine; Andrea
  Wahlstrom, M.V.; Karin Mau (?) M.V.; Cathy Allen, M.V.; Pat Bush, M.V.; Wendy
  Bucknum, M.V.; Norman Malik, M.V.; Chuck Costello, M.V.; July Tully, M.V.; Joe Tully,
  M.V.; Ahlam Bazzi, M.V.; Megan Webb, M.V.; Peggy Russo, M.V.; Matt Corrigan, M.V.;
  Casey Ackerman, M.V.; Helen Workun, M.V.; Joan Way, M.V.; Brian Cleugh, Newport
  Beach; Carl Mead, M.V.; Rick Sandzimier, M.V.; Justin Fesler, M.V.; Sharon Campbell,
  M.V.; Saundra Jacobs, M.V.; and K. David Crockett, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the proposed field office site and read a letter from the
  Orange County Employees Association: Frank Flavin, Huntington Beach.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to the proposed location of the
  probation office: Donna Bourassa, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to authorize
  Mayor Kelley to send a letter to the Orange County Board of Supervisors based on

City Council Minutes  4  September 2, 2014
   comments and public input received at the Council Meeting and incorporating staff and
  Council Member concerns.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 9:00 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:21
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

7.  R. Hero Sculpture Donation at La Paws Park

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her opposition to the sculpture and stated that she feels
  it makes a mockery of 9/11 and the first responders.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to accept
  the R. Hero Sculpture Dalmatian Dog Donation from the Non-Profit Group R- Hero and
  Rick & Bunni Benaron and authorize staff to install the dog sculpture at La Paws Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended, on page 8, to include that the
  Council directed that conceptual design for bocce ball courts will be less than $10,000.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 18, 2014, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  September 2, 2014
 5.  Traffic Signal Maintenance-Battery Back-Up Systems

  Council Member Schlicht stated that a few years ago, a power outage alerted the City to
  non-working backup batteries. She asked if there is a maintenance contract in place now
  and if the backup systems are checked on a regular basis.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon confirmed that the City reworded the maintenance
  contract to provide more regular testing of the batteries and to include a more proactive
  battery replacement program.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  award contract to Aegis ITS, Inc., in the amount of $98,784.00 to provide and install 11 new
  traffic signal battery back-up systems; and (2) adopt Resolution 14-41 Amending the Fiscal
  Year 2014-15 Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: requested that Mayor Kelley give a report to the public
  regarding the judge's reasoning for rejection of the OCFA's equitable adjustment lawsuit
  against the County. He stated that Mission Viejo's hypothetical share of the
  OCFA unfunded liability is $24 million and he asked why that wasn't made public. Finally,
  Mr. Wontrobski questioned the City Attorney's statement that the City is not responsible for
  that liability and he asked for a written opinion on the matter.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

10.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

11.  Orange County Vector Control District

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report and shared a video that he created on West
  Nile virus.

12.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.
City Council Minutes  6  September 2, 2014
 13.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that at the last City Council Meeting, the City Manager didn't
feel that the City Attorney needed to supply additional background information on the new
Assistant City Attorney. He again requested that the Assistant City Attorney provide a resume or
additional information so the public can determine if this person is qualified or not. Mr.
Wontrobski noted that he has written a letter for the 6th time regarding Council Member Ury
showing anger against him and other public speakers.

City Manager Wilberg discussed the report that he gave at the last meeting regarding the
presentation that he and Director of Administrative Services Dyas heard at the Orange County
Employees Retirement System meeting. He noted that he made hard copies of the report and left
them in the Council Members offices. Mr. Wilberg said that there is an illustrative graphic on
page 4 of the presentation that relates to a couple of questions that came up earlier with comments
made by Wontrobski. The graphic clearly shows that the unfunded liability is the responsibility
of either the County of Orange or OCFA and that the contract cities are not responsible for any
unfunded liabilities. Mr. Wilberg announced that he will be at a conference in two weeks so he
will not be at the next City Council Meeting but Assistant City Manager Rattay will be present.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended 8/19/14 to 9/2/14

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

15.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended 7/8/14 to 8/18/14

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon thanked resident Bob Hayes for a great presentation on the Star
Spangled Banner and for sharing Whitney Houston’s rendition of the song. She announced that
Mission Viejo has a Homeowner’s Guide for water conservation, drought tolerant plants and
artificial turf and she encouraged residents to pick up a copy if they are looking to make the
City Council Minutes  7  September 2, 2014
 transition to artificial grass. She also noted that the water companies currently have a lot of rebates
in place. Council Member Reardon reminded residents of the Mission for the Armed Forces
football game on September 12 and the Vietnam vets “welcome home” event where the Girl Scouts
and Boy Scouts will line the road to the community center to symbolically welcome the vets’
home. Council Member Reardon announced that earlier this evening, she and Assistant City
Manager Rattay attended the executive committee meeting of the Emerald Point HOA where they
clarified some confusion on the Special Fire Protection Area and Fuel Modification Zones. She
announced that resident Norm Rozencrans’ son Michael and his wife have now finished putting
together a library where they live in Nepal, thanks to many generous donations from Mission
Viejo. She also outlined new businesses in town including Sperry Topsider and Other Mothers
and she reminded residents that the City will host a Business Expo on September 10 at the Murray
Center. In conclusion, Council Member Reardon shared a video highlight of the new four-part
series on prescription drug abuse, The Invisible Line. She thanked her colleagues and City
Manager Wilberg for their support and Eric Winter, Robert Schick and Tammy Descsoteaux for
doing such a great job to create the program. She noted that the video series is receiving a lot of
attention and is available for viewing on the City’s YouTube Channel. She stated that there are a
lot of people affected by prescription drug abuse and recently more than 300 people attended a
screening of Behind the Orange Curtain in Mission Viejo, so the word is getting out.

Council Member Schlicht

26.  Special Fire Protection Area - Historical Record

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report and stated that the Council majority wronged
  the community in voting for a Special Fire Protection Area and she distributed a packet of
  information labeled Exhibit 17.

27. Adoption of a Resolution Opposing the Implementation of Toll Lanes on I-405 and all
  other Orange County Freeways without a Vote of the Entire Orange County Electorate

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to adopt Resolution 14-XX Opposing
  Implementation of Toll Lanes on I-405 and all other Orange County Freeways without a
  vote of the entire Orange County Electorate. The motion died for lack of a second.

Continuing her statements on the OCTA, Council Member Schlicht said that it is apples to oranges
to compare a toll lane to a toll road. She stated that toll lanes have not been very successful and
that’s why they’ve had to refinance and it’s time for someone to stand up and say “stop the double
taxation.” Council Member Schlicht informed her colleagues that a new Obama rule could force
the City to house illegal aliens if the City accepts CDBG money and she will leave some
information with the City Clerk for the record. She also expressed concern about the appeal at the
last Council meeting and she stated that it was unethical for a Council Member to be driven around
by a Code Enforcement officer, making uninvited visits to businesses. She stated that it is
imperative that government officials know their roles and that they do not breach their authority.
Council Member Schlicht noted that there were no findings to pull that business owner’s CUP and
City Council Minutes  8  September 2, 2014
 she hopes that in the future, the Council doesn’t take personal biases and work against the business
community. Council Member Schlicht stated that she voted against the statue at La Paws Dog
Park because she doesn’t see the dignity in it and it diminishes the sacrifices of those who died on
9/11. She also stated that a probation office is not a good fit for Mission Viejo. This is a family-
oriented community and the Council should jealously strive to protect the quality of life. She
expressed her pride in seeing the community come out strong in opposition to the proposal.
Council Member Schlicht noted that she will leave some information with the City Clerk on the
Common Core curriculum and she announced that parents can submit an opt-out form so their
children do not have to participate in some of the more sensitive areas. She encouraged residents
to educate themselves on the subject. In closing, Council Member Schlicht read a quote from the
National Anthem: “Whose broad stripes and bright stars thru the perilous fight, o'er the ramparts
we watched were so gallantly streaming.”

16.  City Council Minutes

  Due to the late hour, this item was continued to the next City Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  9  September 2, 2014
   Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

25.  Destruction of Records -- Citywide 2013 Records Purge

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury thanked Council Member Reardon for bringing up and continuing to keep
vigilance on the prescription drug abuse epidemic. He noted that she has made it a passion and
she has definitely made an impact by making people aware of the issues. Council Member Ury
stated that the same arguments and discussions come up over and over again and he encouraged
Council Member Reardon to continue to share information on the Special Fire Protection Area and
to keep the discussion alive. He noted that the easiest way to synopsize it is to say that our rules
are better than the State’s and we get to take credit for it.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that the former City Talk with the Mayor is now called Mission Viejo
Today and the newest program covers the topic of the Community of Character program. The
show is currently available on the City’s website and YouTube channel. Mayor Kelley reminded
residents of the upcoming Stand Up for Cancer event on Friday September 5 and a blood drive on
Friday September 12 from 1:00 to 6:15 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at city hall. She encouraged
residents to make an appointment at redcrossblood.org or to contact her for assistance. Mayor
Kelley noted that the City has a wonderful partnership with AYSO Region 84 who co-sponsor the
blood drives; they really help to spread the word and get great participation. Finally, Mayor Kelley
announced that the City will host a Patriot Day ceremony September 11 at 5:30 p.m. to honor the
men, women and children who risked or lost their lives on 9/11.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:58 p.m. with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Frank Ury Senior to Monday, September 15,
2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 15, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  September 2, 2014
